Synthetic Study toward Saccharomicin Based upon Asymmetric
Metal Catalysis
Bhawna Barpuzary, Mijin Kim, and Young Ho Rhee *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 5969 −5972 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Here, we report a de novo metal-catalyzed approach
toward the stereoselective glycosidic bond formation in saccha-
romicin. The signature step is highlighted by the Pd-catalyzed
asymmetric coupling of ene-alkoxyallenes and highly functionalized
alcohol substrates. The reaction showed high chemo-, regio-, and
ligand-driven diastereoselectivity. In combination with the ring-
closing metathesis and late-stage functionalization, this method led
to highly e ﬃcient synthesis of saccharosamine −rhamnose and rhamnose −fucose fragments.
S
accharomicins A and B were ﬁrst isolated in 1998 from
actinomycetes Saccharothrix espanaensis .1 These natural
products showed signi ﬁcant activities against various Gram-
positive and Gram-negative bacteria as well as methicillin-
resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Thus, saccharomicins
and their smaller structural analogues have the potential to be
new antibacterial therapeutics. Chemical synthesis may play a
signiﬁcant role in providing candidates that help to explore
structure−activity relationships of the saccharomicin and to
delineate the mode of action.
From a structural viewpoint, saccharomicin A represents
heptadecasaccharide linked to N-(m,p-dihydroxycinnamoyl)
taurine aglycone. The oligosaccharide moiety in saccharomicin
highlights the longest oligosaccharide found in any natural
products. It consists of ﬁve deoxysugar monosaccharides
including β-
D-3-methyl-3-amino-2,6-dideoxysugars (saccharos-
amine), β-D-fucose, α-L-rhamnose, α-L-digitoxose, and α-L-3-
epivancosamine. The daunting structure and interesting bio-
logical activities of saccharomicins have attracted signi ﬁcant
attention from the synthetic community. A number of strategies
have been developed to prepare for fragments of saccharomi-
cin,
2−5 which mostly focused on the preparation of the core
trisaccharide structure consisting of saccharosamine −rham-
nose−fucose (Sac-Rha-Fuc in Scheme 1). We recently reported
Pd-catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkoxylation of alkoxyallene,
which successfully evolved into the unique synthesis of
numerous 2-deoxyoligosaccharides as well as rare sugars with
no need of activating groups.
6 Here, we report that glycosidic
bonds abundant in saccharomicin (I and II in Scheme 1) could
be constructed by this de novo method in a highly e ﬃcient
manner. For example, Pd-catalyzed coupling reaction of readily
available homoallylic alcohol A and ene-alkoxyallene B
produced dihydropyran intermediate C, wherein the thermo-
dynamically less stable β-stereochemistry was driven by the
chiral ligand. Variation of the alkoxyallene structure in
combination with the oxidative cyclization of carbamate derived
from C delivered the disaccharide form of saccharosamine D
linked to α-
L-rhamnoside. Furthermore, analogous Pd-catalyzed
coupling of unprotected β-D-fucose E and ene-alkoxyallene F
built up the disaccharide G with high stereo- and regioselectivity.
At the outset of the study, we explored the synthesis of
compound 7a, a key precursor to β-D-saccharosamine (Table 1).
We ﬁrst envisioned that the intermediate acyclic acetal4a can be

accessed by the Pd-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of readily
available alcohol 17 and alkoxyallene 2 in the presence of
standard Trost-type ligand 3. However, this reaction generated
4a in only low (<20%) yield (for the detailed information, see
the Supporting Information ). Thus, we switched to an
alternative method combining ene-alkoxyallene 5 and alcohol
6. When an equimolar amount of these compounds was reacted
in toluene at 40 °C for 24 h in the presence of Pd 2(dba)3 (2.5
mol %), (S,S)-3 (5 mol %), and a small amount of triethylamine,
4a was obtained in signi ﬁcantly higher 36% yield (entry 1).
Employing excess allene 5 (2 equiv) generated 4a in higher yield
(entry 2). Further improvement of the yield was seen with the
use of excess alcohol 6 (entry 3). Finally, increasing the loading
of the precatalyst Pd
2(dba)3 (5 mol %) generated 4a in 65%
yield (entry 4). In this case, the subsequent RCM reaction using
5 mol % of second-generation Hoveyda −Grubbs catalyst
provided the desired product 7a in 52% yield over two steps
with 8:1 stereoselectivity. The use of enantiomeric ligand (R,R)-
3 inverted the stereochemical outcome, generating 7b in 90%
yield with <1:25 stereoselectivity (entry 5). This result is
consistent with our previous reports on various hydro-
alkoxylation reactions. Thus, the chiral-ligand-driven stereo-
control at the anomeric center worked well with sterically bulky
allene 5. The structure of 7a was rigorously conﬁrmed by various
NMR techniques (for the detailed analysis, see the Supporting
Information).
The next task was to synthesize 10 possessing all the
stereochemical features of β-
D-saccharosamine from the
intermediate 7a using the oxidative cyclization by way of the
carbamate intermediate.2a,8 For this purpose, the benzyl group
in 7a was ﬁrst removed by Na/NH3 to give the alcohol 8 in 93%
yield. From this compound, carbamate 9 was uneventfully
prepared in 90% yield by the reaction with p-methoxyphenyl
isocyanate and DBU in CH2Cl2 at rt. The oxidative cyclization of
9 was conducted by heating with 2-iodoxybenzoic acid (IBX)
and NaHCO3 in DMSO:THF (10:1) at 90 °C, which produced
the target 10 in 61% yield as a single diastereomer. Thus, the
stereochemical purity of theβ-glycosidic bond was not eroded in
this oxidative cyclization.
Having established a protocol for the monosaccharide form of
saccharomicin, we then expanded the reaction to the synthesis of
saccharosamine-rhamnose disaccharide 17 (I in Scheme 1). For
this purpose, allene 5 was reacted with readily available allylic
alcohol 11 (2 equiv) possessing the stereochemistry found in the
natural product. As depicted in Scheme 3, the asymmetric Pd-
catalyzed coupling reaction turned out to be considerably faster
than that of cyclohexanol 6 described in Table 1. In this case, the
acyclic O,O-acetal 12a was formed in near-quantitative isolated
yield in the presence of 3.5 mol % of Pd
2(dba)3 and 7 mol % of
ligand ( S,S)-3 as a single stereoisomer. 9 This compound was
then treated with second-generation Hoveyda−Grubb’s catalyst
(5 mol %) to provide the biscyclic intermediate13a in 79% yield
with no erosion of the stereochemical purity. Notably,
potentially competing ring-rearrangement metathesis (RRM)
was not observed in this reaction.
10 Then, we employed the
enantiomeric ( R,R)-3 ligand to determine the chiral ligand-
driven stereoselectivity in the Pd-catalyzed reaction. In this case,
diastereomeric 13b was obtained again as a single stereoisomer
by way of 12b in 86% yield over two steps. The NMR spectrum
of 13a was clearly distinguishable from that of 13b, thus
conﬁrming the stereoselectivity described above (for the details
of the analysis, see the Supporting Information).
Synthesis of the disaccharide 17 requires late-stage chemo-
selective dihydroxylation that can distinguish two oleﬁn moieties
in 13a. We reasoned that this selectivity could be easily induced
by the contrasting stereochemical feature of anomeric centers.
Indeed, subjection of the compound 13a to the Upjohn
dihydroxylation condition
11 using OsO 4 (3 mol %) and N-
methylmorpholine oxide (1.3 equiv) generated diol 14 in 81%
yield as a single compound with complete chemo- and
stereoselectivity. The subsequent treatment of diol 14 by
methoxymethyl chloride (MOMCl) provided 15 in 89% yield.
Synthesis of fully functionalized disaccharide 17 from 15
proceeded uneventfully using the protocol developed in Scheme
2. Thus, removal of the benzyl group using Na/NH
3 (93% yield)
followed by treatment with DBU and p-methoxyphenyl
isocyanate produced carbamate 16 in 83% yield. This
compound was heated with IBX in DMSO:THF (10:1) in the
presence of NaHCO
3, in a sealed tube at 90°C to give 17 in 75%
yield (Scheme 3).
Having prepared the saccharosamine−rhamnose disaccharide
moiety, our ﬁnal eﬀorts were directed at the construction of the
glycosidic-bond -connecting fucose −rhamnose disaccharide

moiety (II in Scheme 1 ). This reaction necessitates selective
coupling reaction at C 3−OH of β-D-fucoside. Preliminary tests
using the substrate 18 equipped with protective groups at other
hydroxyl groups and the allene 196d showed the formation of an
adduct in only trace yield, presumably due to the steric
congestion of the substrate 18 (Scheme 4). Remarkably, the use
of unprotected triol 20 signiﬁcantly improved the result. For
example, the use of 20 (1 equiv) and slight excess of 19 (1.1
equiv) in the presence of Pd 2(dba)3 (2.5 mol %), ligand (S,S)-3
(5 mol %), and triethylamine (0.1 equiv) generated the desired
compound 21a in 76% yield after RCM reaction along with a
small amount of regioisomers ( ∼13% combined yield). In this
case, the stereoisomer 21b was obtained only in trace amount.
Employing enantiomeric ligand ( R,R)-3 provided 21b in 87%
yield with the formation of regio- and stereoisomers in a trace
amount.
12 The regiochemical outcome of the reaction was
conﬁrmed by the extensive NMR studies of bisbenzoate 22,
which could be readily prepared from 21. (For the detailed
information on the synthesis and analysis of 22, see the
Supporting Information .) The ﬁnal dihydroxylation reaction
went smoothly to provide the tetrol 23 in 90% yield as a single
diastereomer.
In summary, we have developed a de novo synthetic method
toward saccharomicin representing a formidable challenge in
deoxyoligosaccharide synthesis. The unique regio-, chemo-, and
stereoselectivities address the utility of various metal-catalyzed
reactions in this endeavor. Currently, we are working on the
development of convergent synthetic strategies aiming at the
total synthesis of saccharomicin. The results of this study will be
reported in due course.
